ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure connects multiple vertical branches by two upper and lower common rails. The leftmost branch is a 10 A current source, with the arrow upward; the middle branch is a 5 Ω resistor; further to the right is a switch branch, marked with a downward current i(t), and the switch closes at t=0; the rightmost branch is a 5 Ω resistor in series with a 2.5 H inductor. All these vertical branches are connected between the same pair of upper and lower rails. Reasoning: When t<0, the switch has been open for a long time, and the circuit is in DC steady state, so the inductor is equivalent to a short circuit. Therefore the middle 5 Ω branch and the right-side 5 Ω + inductor branch are equivalent to two 5 Ω resistors in parallel, powered by the 10 A current source. The two parallel resistors are equal, so the current is divided equally, and the current in each branch is 5 A, in the direction from top to bottom. Therefore the inductor current i_L(0-)=5 A, and the inductor current is continuous, so i_L(0+)=5 A. When t>0, the switch closes, short-circuiting the upper and lower rails, and the rail voltage is 0. The voltage across the middle 5 Ω resistor is 0, so its current is 0. The right-side RL branch satisfies 2.5 di_L/dt + 5 i_L = 0, so i_L(t)=5e^{-(5/2.5)t}=5e^{-2t} A. Writing KCL for the upper rail: the 10 A current source injects current into the upper rail, and this current is divided into the switch current i(t) and the right-side branch inductor current i_L(t), while the middle branch current is 0. Therefore i(t)=10-i_L(t)=10-5e^{-2t}. At t=0.5 s, i(0.5)=10-5e^{-1}=10-1.8394=8.1606 A, approximately 8.16 A.

The two 5 Ω branches are then in parallel across the 10 A source, so each carries 5 A downward; hence i_L(0-)=i_L(0+)=5 A. For t>0, the closed switch forces the rail voltage to zero, so the center 5 Ω current is zero and the right RL branch obeys 2.5 di_L/dt + 5 i_L = 0, giving i_L(t)=5e^{-2t}. Apply KCL at the top rail: 10 A supplied by the source equals switch current plus right-branch inductor current, so i(t)=10-5e^{-2t}. Evaluate at t=0.5 s to get i(0.5)=10-5e^{-1}=8.16 A.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that before switching the inductor branch and the middle 5 Ω resistor are parallel load branches driven by the 10 A source. Since the switch has been open for a long time, the inductor is a short at DC, making the two load resistances both 5 Ω; by equal current division the right branch/inductor current is initially 5 A downward. After the switch closes, the switch has zero resistance and bypasses the resistor network, so the rail voltage and the final current in the RL branch are 0 A. The right branch therefore has a natural decay from 5 A to 0 A with time constant τ=L/R=2.5/5=0.5 s: i_L(t)=5e^{-t/0.5}. The 10 A current source current must split between the switch and the decaying RL branch, while the shunt resistor has zero voltage and no current; hence the labeled switch current is i(t)=10-i_L(t). At t=0.5 s, i(t)=10-5e^{-1}=8.16 A.

Image description: The circuit in the figure connects multiple vertical branches by two upper and lower common rails. The leftmost branch is a 10 A current source, with the arrow upward; the middle branch is a 5 Ω resistor; further to the right is a switch branch, labeled with a downward current i(t), and the switch closes at t=0; the rightmost branch is a 5 Ω resistor in series with a 2.5 H inductor. All these vertical branches are connected between the same pair of upper and lower rails.

Reasoning: When t<0, the switch has been open for a long time, and the circuit is in DC steady state, so the inductor is equivalent to a short circuit. Therefore the middle 5 Ω branch and the right 5 Ω+inductor branch are equivalent to two 5 Ω resistors in parallel, powered by the 10 A current source. The two parallel resistors are equal, so the current divides equally, and the current in each branch is 5 A, in the direction from top to bottom. Therefore the inductor current i_L(0-)=5 A, and the inductor current is continuous, so i_L(0+)=5 A.

When t>0, the switch closes, short-circuiting the upper and lower rails, and the rail voltage is 0. The voltage across the middle 5 Ω resistor is 0, so its current is 0. The right RL branch satisfies 2.5 di_L/dt + 5 i_L = 0, so i_L(t)=5e^{-(5/2.5)t}=5e^{-2t} A.

Write KCL at the upper rail: the 10 A current source injects into the upper rail, and this current is divided into the switch current i(t) and the inductor current i_L(t) in the right branch, while the middle branch current is 0. Therefore i(t)=10-i_L(t)=10-5e^{-2t}. At t=0.5 s, i(0.5)=10-5e^{-1}=10-1.8394=8.1606 A, approximately 8.16 A.
